headline: High risk of shared-workspace data leakage and write conflicts; Dify→Replit output chaining can also cascade errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can write filesystem content and uses uploaded knowledge base files; Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where one agent’s file output can be treated as instructions by the other. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so I rate this medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Dify writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file that Replit Agent later reads as guidance
IF Replit Agent ingests file contents without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces or directories
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into prompts
Add a manual review step before either agent reads the other's outputs
Use provenance tags in filenames and prompts
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization and trust-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, and both can persist data in shared server-side or Repl storage. That makes sensitive data exposure plausible in default use, with blast radius including secrets and logs.
conditions: IF either agent stores sensitive files in a workspace the other can read
IF either agent forwards file contents or logs to its backend or external APIs
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Rotate any credentials exposed to either agent
Restrict network egress to approved endpoints
Use separate storage roots for knowledge base and Repl files
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls and audit logging

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write filesystems, and use broad network egress; Replit Agent also modifies git state. In a shared directory, concurrent writes and repository changes can collide without locking, causing destructive overwrites or inconsistent deployments. The overlap is substantial and dangerous by default if they operate on the same project.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Replit Agent commits or rewrites files while Dify is also generating artifacts
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Review diffs before applying changes
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can emit tool-driven outputs, and Replit Agent is a planner that acts inside a Repl with user checkpoints. If Replit consumes Dify’s output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into code or deployment changes. The checkpointing lowers risk, but the pathway still exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses Dify-generated instructions or code without independent verification
IF Dify outputs are copied into Replit tasks or prompts
mitigations: Require a human review of Dify outputs before Replit acts on them
Ask Replit Agent to restate assumptions before execution
Limit Dify output to summaries instead of executable steps
Compare generated changes against expected diffs
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs and knowledge base content, while Replit Agent touches secrets and deployment configuration. The profiles do not document aligned retention, residency, or deletion controls, so mixed handling of the same data class can create compliance mismatch. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined storage and handling patterns.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents’ storage or logs
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between Dify and Replit environments
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent
Document retention and deletion settings for both systems
Separate regulated workloads from general workloads
Review vendor terms for residency and logging
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
